The reproduction I have for this issue: opencode's catalog only sees the static snapshot at `https://models.dev/api.json`. NVIDIA's NIM, however, has had GLM-5.1 and GLM-5.2 (and many other models) live for a while — I just confirmed:

- `GET https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/models` returns `z-ai/glm-5.2`
- It also serves `moonshotai/kimi-k2.6`, `minimaxai/minimax-m3`, `mistralai/mistral-medium-3.5-128b`, `qwen/qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct`, etc.

None of these are reflected in opencode's desktop model picker because `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/nvidia.ts` only injects HTTP tracking headers — it does not populate models. The `NvidiaPlugin` itself never reads from NIM's `/v1/models`; it relies entirely on `packages/core/src/models-dev.ts` → models.dev.

So for users who pick `provider: nvidia`, missing models is by construction: until z-ai publishes to models.dev, the GLM models simply aren't selectable.

A clean fix would be one of:

1. Live merge: NVIDIA plugin fetches `/v1/models` on catalog build and overlays on top of `models.dev` entries.
2. Opt-in flag: `OPENCODE_NVIDIA_LIVE_MODELS=1` enables (1).
3. Quick workaround in `~/.config/opencode/config.json`: define `provider.nvidia.models` manually so the catalog picks them up without touching the binary.

Happy to send a PR for (1) or (2) if a maintainer can confirm the preferred direction.

**Update — the affected code has moved, but the bug is still present on `dev`.**

Since this was filed, `provider.ts` was refactored: `resolveEntryPoint` is no longer in `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts`. Provider now resolves entrypoints via `Npm.add(...)` and reads `item.entrypoint`. The resolution logic itself was relocated to `packages/core/src/npm.ts`.

The bug came along with it unchanged. Current `dev`, `packages/core/src/npm.ts:53`:

```ts
entrypoint = typeof Bun !== "undefined" ? import.meta.resolve(name, dir) : import.meta.resolve(dir)
```

Same asymmetry as originally reported: the Bun branch uses the two-arg `import.meta.resolve(name, dir)`, while the Node branch uses the one-arg `import.meta.resolve(dir)`, which resolves to the package **directory** URL and throws `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT` under Node/Electron. The caller (`Npm.add`) passes the package directory in as `dir`, so the broken path is still reached and the original repro still applies on Desktop.

The proposed fix still holds — it just needs to target the new file. Using the two-arg form on both paths (`import.meta.resolve(name, dir)`) resolves the package export correctly on both Bun and Node 20.6+.

Note that #32060 ("fix(core): resolve npm provider entrypoints", *Closes #31909*) covers this but is **still open / unmerged**, so anyone hitting this on `dev` should look at `packages/core/src/npm.ts` rather than the old `provider.ts` path.

Following up on my own issue: as of v1.17.x the new server API (`packages/server`, mounted by `opencode serve`) appears to supersede this request, in a stronger form than what I proposed:

- `POST /api/session/{sessionID}/prompt` no longer blocks for the full run — it returns `200` with a `SessionInputAdmitted` receipt: `{ admittedSeq, id, sessionID, prompt, delivery, timeCreated }`. The body also accepts a caller-supplied `id`, with duplicate detection against the durable store (`ConflictError`), which gives idempotent sends.
- `GET /api/session/{sessionID}/history?after=<seq>` exposes a durable, sequenced event log (`SessionDurableEvent[]`). `session.next.prompt.admitted` carries the user `messageID`, and `session.next.step.started` / `session.next.text.ended` carry the `assistantMessageID`.

So the correlation recipe is: send prompt → take `admittedSeq` from the receipt → poll `history?after=admittedSeq` → read `assistantMessageID` off the step events. I verified this end-to-end against `ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode:1.17.13` and it works exactly as described. This is better than the pre-allocated-ID approach I proposed (durable, resumable, safe under concurrency, no SSE required).

Two questions before this can be closed:
1. Is the `/api/session/*` surface considered stable for server-to-server integrations, or still subject to breaking changes?
2. Is the legacy `prompt_async` (`204 No Content`) path planned for deprecation, or will it remain the non-correlatable fire-and-forget option?

Happy to close this if the V2 flow is the intended answer.

Opened a fix for this in #35245 against `dev`.

The hang is one path: V1 waited on Node's `close` event, which never fires when grandchildren inherit stdio. V2 (the core bash tool) wraps the read loop in `Effect.scoped` and bounds it with `Effect.timeoutOrElse`. V1 still had the V0 raceAll/handle.kill shape.

This PR mirrors V2 in V1. The spawner's `acquireRelease` finalizer sends SIGTERM on scope cleanup. When `Effect.timeoutOrElse` cancels, the `Deferred.await` is interrupted cleanly. Pipes free, error propagates, bug-shape can't occur.

I also created a companion plugin at https://github.com/Levosilimo/opencode-shell-hang-guard that rewrites `pkill -f` to a basename-guarded variant. Useful until this PR ships, optional afterward.

Same issue here -- clean reproduction path identified.

**Environment:**
- Switched from running opencode source (plugin @opencode-ai/plugin@1.17.11) to Homebrew-installed v1.17.13
- macOS arm64, terminal (TUI) usage

**Timeline of the wipe:**
The first launch of v1.17.13 ran 38 database schema migrations in a single batch at the same timestamp. The critical migration:

`20260622170816_reset_v2_session_state`

explicitly cleared all existing session state. After it ran, the project record was created fresh and the first new session started seconds later. Every file under `~/.local/share/opencode/` was recreated between 20:17-20:37, with nothing surviving from before.

**Evidence from opencode.db:**
- All 38 migrations have the same `time_completed` timestamp: `1783120735232`
- Migration `reset_v2_session_state` ran at `1783120735246` (14ms after migrations started)
- Project record created at `1783120735366` (122ms after)
- The old project record (from previous version) was gone
- `data_migration` table was empty

**Root cause:**
Migration `20260622170816_reset_v2_session_state` -- shipped between the user's previous version and v1.17.13 -- is destructive on existing session data when triggered. It should either be a no-op when sessions already exist, or the auto-update path should back up the DB before running migrations.

**Suggestion for fix:**
1. Before running destructive migrations, copy `opencode.db` to `opencode.db.pre-migration` as a safety net
2. Design migration `reset_v2_session_state` to detect pre-existing data and skip or merge instead of dropping
3. Document in release notes that this migration will clear session history

I've been thinking for a long time to make the task_id return even if the agent stalls out, errors, etc. Just too many higher priority issues to work on. A fix is needed. The recovery pattern for agents is typically trying to resume the session and observing it fail without understanding why, and then just retasking a fresh subagent. 

Which works, but its sometimes inefficient and creates more token burn. The additional feature that's needed though is for when subagents fail to return, due to interruption or an error (such as a connection timeout), relaying the error message or the last section of text and message type (e.g. an agent was interrupted or stalled out with last messages being thinking blocks). 

That way the tasking agent can have enough information to better infer and understand why the subagent failed to return, and initiate more appropriate recovery processes.  This would help make more autonomous workflows; less need for humans to help agents understand why a subagent session failed to return. 

I'd suggest expanding the scope of the fix as needed to fully address matters.
